item.description:
A review of every setting in the four security tiers: fixes where a tier didn't do what it said, and better defaults.
### Fixed - **ZTH Ebook:** newly registered and revived domains now get their caution page (a block rule above it used to catch them first). AI apps get a caution page with uploads blocked, as the tier describes, instead of being blocked outright. The crypto rule, which blocked an unrelated category, is gone: crypto exchanges are categorized as Finance, and the checklist says how to block them. Its AI caution rule, which applied to general IT sites, is gone too. - **Strict and ZTH Ebook** no longer block every collaboration app, so Zoom, Teams and Webex keep working. - **ZTH Ebook** now includes the Malware Protection and Advanced Settings steps, with Strict's values. - **Strict and Balanced** require TLS 1.2 on inspected traffic. Strict blocks untrusted server certificates; Balanced passes them through to the browser's warning. - **Permissive** keeps domain fronting and CONNECT/SNI mismatch protection, and applies firewall rules to remote users.
### Changed - **Permissive** is minimal again: no blocks on executable downloads, file sharing, personal webmail or social posts. Uncategorized sites get a caution page and remote access tools are allowed. Office files and executables are scanned in the Sandbox without holding them. It has no DLP rules, since it doesn't inspect SSL, and Review lists the rules that apply to unencrypted HTTP only. - **Balanced:** - Uncategorized sites open in Browser Isolation (a caution page without it), and remote access tools get a caution page. - Executables are held in the Sandbox until analyzed instead of blocked. - Only Windows script downloads are blocked. - DNS tunnels are blocked only in the risky categories. - The firewall blocks P2P and tunneling apps. - File sharing and webmail block only uploads and attachments. - **Strict:** - The firewall's default deny now lets through only web, NTP, meetings (including the STUN traffic calls use), ICMP and OCSP; SSH and RDP to the internet need a rule of your own. - Executables are held in the Sandbox. - Health and finance sites aren't inspected. - **News sites** are no longer in the Bandwidth Loss rules (blocked in Strict, a caution page in Balanced). - **DLP:** HIPAA and PII rules need a Social Security number together with medical information or names, instead of either one alone. The PCI rule looks for card numbers only, and the resume rule for resumes only. - **Malware Protection** lists a Suspicious Content Protection (PageRisk) threshold for each tier. - **Policy Simulator:** a PAC file over 2 MB is refused as it downloads, and CSV exports also neutralize cells that start with a tab or carriage return.
